content: The progression of Type 1 Diabetes, as outlined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), includes distinct stages. In Stage 2 of Type 1 Diabetes, individuals exhibit the presence of autoantibodies, which are markers of an autoimmune response targeting the insulin-producing beta cells of the pancreas. At this stage, there is evidence of dysglycemia, meaning abnormal glucose levels are detected through testing. However, individuals in this stage do not yet display any clinical symptoms of diabetes.
